prompt: This year is 2021. In how many years will it be 2223?
If $A\times 4=B$ and $B-A=33$, then what is the value of $A$?
What is the value of $x$ in the diagram? (The two horizontal lines are parallel.)

solutions.title: Parallel lines
solutions.body:
Through the vertex marked $x^\circ$ draw a line parallel to the two given lines. The top part of $x$ equals the alternate angle $26^\circ$. The bottom part equals the alternate angle to the interior angle next to $130^\circ$, which is $180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$. So $x=26+50=76$.

**Answer: 76**

prompt: The solid shown is formed by taking a $3\text{ cm}\times3\text{ cm}\times3\text{ cm}$ cube and 'drilling' a $1\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ square hole from the centre of each face to the centre of the opposite face. What is the volume in $\text{cm}^3$ of the solid?

solutions.title: Count unit cubes
solutions.body:
The cube is made of 27 unit cubes. Drilling removes the centre cube of each of the 6 faces and the cube in the very middle: $6+1=7$ cubes. Volume $=27-7=20\text{ cm}^3$.

**Answer: 20**

prompt: Each of the ten paths shown is 1 metre long. An ant walks along the paths from A to B without going along any path more than once. What is the length (in metres) of the longest possible route?

solutions.title: Parity argument
solutions.body:
Every path used by the ant adds 1 to the number of times a vertex is touched, so any vertex that is not A or B must have an even number of used paths, while A and B have an odd number. A and B each have 2 paths, so one path at each must be unused. The two vertices on the upper left and upper right of the middle each have 3 paths, so each must have at least one unused path. Hence at least 2 paths are unused (the path at A and the one at the upper left can coincide, and so can those at B and upper right), so the route has length at most 8. It is achieved by A, lower left, middle, upper left, top, upper right, middle, lower right, B.

**Answer: 8**

prompt: If the three numbers along each diagonal are added, the average of these sums is 25. Determine the value of $x$.

solutions.title: Use the four diagonals
solutions.body:
The four diagonals through the centre each contain $x$ and a pair of opposite numbers. Opposite pairs are $(1,8),(2,7),(3,6),(4,5)$, each with sum 9. So each diagonal sums to $9+x$. The average is $9+x=25$, so $x=16$.

**Answer: 16**

prompt: I want to write a list of consecutive positive integers starting with 1. The list must contain three square numbers and three cube numbers. What is the smallest number of integers that could be in my list?

solutions.title: List them
solutions.body:
The squares start $1,4,9,\dots$ and the cubes $1,8,27,\dots$. To contain three cubes the list must reach 27. Up to 27 it contains the squares $1,4,9,16,25$ and the cubes $1,8,27$, so 27 integers suffice and are needed.

**Answer: 27**

prompt: A rectangular sheet of paper has dimensions 10 cm by 15 cm. From this sheet, twelve 1 cm by 1 cm squares are cut out, as shown. What is the perimeter of the resulting shape in cm?

solutions.title: Each notch adds 2 cm
solutions.body:
The original perimeter is $2(10+15)=50$ cm. Cutting a $1\times1$ square from the edge removes 1 cm of edge and adds 3 cm, a net gain of 2 cm. So the perimeter is $50+12\times2=74$ cm.

**Answer: 74**

prompt: The sum of five consecutive positive integers, starting with $n$, is a perfect square. What is the smallest possible value of $n$?

solutions.title: Factor the sum
solutions.body:
The sum is $n+(n+1)+\dots+(n+4)=5n+10=5(n+2)$. For this to be a perfect square, $n+2$ must be $5$ times a square. The smallest is $n+2=5$, so $n=3$ (sum $=25$).

**Answer: 3**

prompt: From the first 100 natural numbers (i.e. 1 to 100 inclusive) all the multiples of 2 are removed, and then all the multiples of 5 are removed. How many numbers are left?

solutions.title: Count
solutions.body:
Removing even numbers leaves the 50 odd numbers. Of these, the multiples of 5 are $5,15,\dots,95$: 10 numbers. $50-10=40$.

**Answer: 40**

solutions.title: Inclusion-exclusion
solutions.body:
Numbers divisible by 2 or 5: $50+20-10=60$, so $100-60=40$ are left.

**Answer: 40**

prompt: All the prime numbers less than 2021 are multiplied together. What is the units digit of this product?

solutions.title: A factor of 10
solutions.body:
The product contains both the primes 2 and 5, so it is divisible by 10 and ends in 0.

**Answer: 0**

prompt: 16 Jelly Tots are arranged in a 4 by 4 square. The Jelly Tots are connected with toothpicks as shown. How many toothpicks would be needed for a 10 by 10 square containing 100 Jelly Tots?

solutions.title: Rows and columns
solutions.body:
Each of the 10 rows needs 9 toothpicks, and each of the 10 columns needs 9 toothpicks. Total $10\times9+10\times9=180$.

**Answer: 180**

prompt: The positive integers $x,y,z$ satisfy $xy=10$, $yz=15$ and $xz=6$. What is the value of $x+y+z$?

solutions.title: Common factor
solutions.body:
$y$ divides both 10 and 15, so $y=1$ or $5$. If $y=1$ then $z=15$ does not divide into $xz=6$. So $y=5$, $z=3$, $x=2$, sum $10$.

**Answer: 10**

prompt: If the pattern continues in the same way, how many shaded blocks will be in Figure 30?

solutions.title: Split into two parts
solutions.body:
The backwards-L shape (right column plus bottom row) has 7, 9, 11 blocks in Figures 1, 2, 3, i.e. $2n+5$ blocks in Figure $n$: $65$ for $n=30$. The diagonal blocks inside number $n+1$: $31$ for $n=30$. Total $65+31=96$.

**Answer: 96**

prompt: The diagram shows three identical squares of side length 8 cm. The top square is exactly centred over the two squares below it. Determine the area of the shaded region in $\text{cm}^2$.

solutions.title: Big triangle minus a corner
solutions.body:
Place the diagonal from the top-left corner of the top square to the bottom-right corner of the bottom row. It spans a width of $12$ (the top square is offset by 4 from the left end) and a height of $16$. The right triangle formed with the right side of the bottom row has area $\frac{12\times16}{2}=96$, but its top part sticks out beside the top square: a $4\times8$ rectangle of area $32$ is not part of the shape. The shaded area is $96-32=64\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: 64**

prompt: The combination for a certain lock is a 4-digit number, with no two adjacent digits the same. How many combinations are possible if the digits are 2, 0, 2, 1?

solutions.title: Place the 2s
solutions.body:
The two 2s cannot be adjacent, so their positions are $(1,3)$, $(1,4)$ or $(2,4)$: 3 ways. The digits 0 and 1 fill the other two places in 2 ways. Total $3\times2=6$.

**Answer: 6**

prompt: The average of 10 scores is 80. When the highest and lowest scores are removed, the average of the remaining scores is 70. What was the average of the two scores that were removed?

solutions.title: Totals
solutions.body:
Total of 10 scores $=800$; total of the remaining 8 is $560$. The two removed sum to $240$, average $120$.

**Answer: 120**

prompt: If $xy-2y=10$ where $x$ and $y$ are positive integers, what is the sum of all possible values of $x$?

solutions.title: Factorise
solutions.body:
$y(x-2)=10$, so $x-2$ is a divisor of 10: $1,2,5,10$ (it must be positive since $y>0$). Then $x=3,4,7,12$ with sum $26$.

**Answer: 26**

prompt: A fruit basket contains bananas and grapes. The ratio of bananas to grapes in the basket is 3:8. When I remove one banana the ratio changes to 1:3. How many grapes are in the basket?

solutions.title: Use a multiplier
solutions.body:
Let there be $3k$ bananas and $8k$ grapes. Then $\frac{3k-1}{8k}=\frac13$ gives $9k-3=8k$, $k=3$. Grapes: $8\times3=24$.

**Answer: 24**

prompt: A rectangle is cut into two regions by a single line from a corner as shown. The areas of the two regions are in the ratio of 1:5. If $a+b=48$ cm, determine the length of $a$.

solutions.title: Triangle is one sixth
solutions.body:
The triangle is $\frac16$ of the rectangle. With rectangle width $w$: $\frac12aw=\frac16\cdot48w$, so $a=16$.

**Answer: 16**

prompt: In the diagram the outer semi-circle has a radius of 2 cm, and the inner semi-circle has a radius of 1 cm. The radii are equally spaced. What percentage of the entire shape is shaded?

solutions.title: Compare areas
solutions.body:
The radii cut the half-disc into 6 equal sectors of $30^\circ$, i.e. $\frac1{12}$ of a full circle each. One shaded piece (ring part) has area $\frac1{12}(\pi\cdot2^2-\pi\cdot1^2)=\frac\pi4$; four are shaded: $\pi$. The whole shape has area $\frac12\pi\cdot2^2=2\pi$. So $\frac{\pi}{2\pi}=50\%$.

**Answer: 50**

prompt: The faces of a fair die are numbered 1 to 6. When the die is rolled, one number will be face-down and the other five numbers will be visible. The probability that 210 is divisible by all of the five visible numbers is $\frac ab$ in simplified form. What is the value of $a+b$?

solutions.title: Which number must be hidden
solutions.body:
$210=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$ is divisible by $1,2,3,5,6$ but not by $4$. So $4$ must be face-down: probability $\frac16$. $a+b=1+6=7$.

**Answer: 7**

prompt: A point inside a square is joined to the midpoint of each side as shown. Three areas are indicated. Determine the area of the unknown region in $\text{cm}^2$.

solutions.title: Join to the vertices
solutions.body:
Join the point to the four vertices. Each side's midpoint splits a triangle into two equal parts, so the regions are paired: with areas $a,b,c,d$ round the figure (small triangles), the opposite regions satisfy $a+d=b+c$ (both equal half the square). Here the three given regions are $16$, $20$, $32$ and the unknown one is opposite $20$: $16+32=20+x$ gives $x=28$.

**Answer: 28**

solutions.title: Total area
solutions.body:
Opposite regions sum to the same amount, namely half the area of the square. So $20+x=16+32=48$, and $x=28$.

**Answer: 28**

prompt: Amara jogs from her home to the beach. When she gets to the beach she immediately turns around and jogs back home again. She is away from home for 2 hours. Her speed going to the beach is 15 km/h, and her speed for the return journey is 10 km/h. How long (in minutes) did it take her to run from home to the beach?

solutions.title: Equal distances
solutions.body:
Let the outward time be $t$ hours: $15t=10(2-t)$, so $25t=20$ and $t=\frac45$ h $=48$ min.

**Answer: 48**

solutions.title: Time ratio
solutions.body:
The distances are equal, so times are in the inverse ratio of the speeds, $10:15=2:3$. The 120 minutes split $2:3$ into 48 and 72, and the faster outward leg is the shorter time: $48$ min.

**Answer: 48**

prompt: When the seven numbers $13;p;16;7;4;15;17$ are arranged in ascending order, the median is the same value as the mean. What is the value of $p$?

solutions.title: Cases
solutions.body:
The six known numbers $4,7,13,15,16,17$ sum to $72$. If $p\le13$ the median is $13$, giving $p=19$, a contradiction. If $13\le p\le15$ the median is $p$: $(72+p)/7=p$ gives $p=12$, a contradiction. If $p\ge15$ the median is $15$: $72+p=105$, $p=33$, which is valid.

**Answer: 33**
